text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- For the first time ever there are more than five million cars on Austria's roads.
- Plans to turn the Post Office's savings bank PSK into a listed company have passed through the parliament's finance commitee.
- Entrepreneurs want to be allowed to buy back shares in their own companies.
- The due diligence examination of bids for Creditanstalt will start on Monday
- Builder Porr hopes for an upturn in Austria's construction industry by 1998 at the latest.
- Jacques Santer, on a visit to Vienna, is certain that European Economic and Monetary Union will start in 1999.
- Shares of Motorbike maker KTM will be listed by December 12, while preferred shares in insolvent constructor Maculan will be delisted today.
DIE PRESSE
- German plans to pull out of the Vienna-based United Nations industrial development body UNIDO could spell its end.
- The coalition government plans to darw up the 1998 and 1999 budgets next year.
- A majority of Austrians are still against the introduction of a single European currency, according to a survey.
- So that the state-owned postal service is able to have an equity capital of 30 percent, its parent holding PTBG will have to take over 48 billion schillings of its debts.
- Steelmaker VA-Stahl is planning on saving 3.5 billion schillings through a special programme. New investments are planned in Eastern Europe and in the car and appliance industries.
KURIER
- Chemical group OMV is planning to cut 200 jobs in its petrochemicals unit next year.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- A new chipcard for Austria's health insurance system will save some 575 million schillings for the economy.
- After a record year for insurers in 1996 due to booming life insurances, expectations for next year are not quite as good.
